citeAs: Vivien Sainte Fare Garnot, Loic Landrieu (2021). Panoptic Segmentation of Satellite Image Time Series with Convolutional Temporal Attention Networks. ICCV 2021.
creator: Vivien Sainte Fare Garnot, Loic Landrieu (LASTIG, Univ. Gustave Eiffel, ENSG, IGN)
description: PASTIS is the first large-scale, publicly available Satellite Image Time Series (SITS) dataset with both semantic and panoptic annotations for agricultural parcel segmentation. It comprises 2,433 sequences of multi-spectral Sentinel-2 images (128×128 pixels, 10 spectral bands, 10m resolution) covering over 4,000 km² across four regions of France, with acquisitions between September 2018 and November 2019. The dataset contains over 2 billion annotated pixels with 124,422 individualized parcels labeled across 18 crop types plus background.
name: PASTIS (Panoptic Agricultural Satellite TIme Series)
publisher: LASTIG, Univ. Gustave Eiffel, ENSG, IGN
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The French Payment Agency estimates the accuracy of the crop annotations via in situ control over 98% and the relative error in terms of surfaces under 0.3%.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were derived from the publicly available French Land Parcel Identification System (FLPIS). Each pixel was annotated with a semantic label corresponding to the parcel's crop type (18 classes) or background. Each unique parcel received an instance label. Parcels whose surface is more than 50% outside the patch extent were annotated with the void label. A 73-class FLPIS nomenclature was reduced to 18 classes by selecting those with at least 400 parcels and samples in at least 2 of the 4 Sentinel-2 tiles.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is highly unbalanced, with a ratio of over 50 between the most and least common classes. To mitigate this, patches were selected favoring those with rare crop types. The dataset covers only four regions of France, which may not represent all climates and crop distributions globally.
rai:dataCollection: Satellite images were collected from the open-access Sentinel-2 platform via the THEIA data cluster. For each of 2,433 patches, all available acquisitions between September 2018 and November 2019 were stacked into a time series. Acquisitions with more than 90% cloud cover were automatically filtered out by the Sentinel data provider. The dataset spans four different Sentinel-2 tiles in different regions of France.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Acquisitions with more than 90% cloud cover were automatically filtered out by the Sentinel data provider THEIA. Even after this filtering, some patches remain partially or completely obstructed by cloud cover (estimated ~28% of images have at least partial cloud cover). No further cloud detection preprocessing was applied; raw data with partial cloud cover is included in PASTIS.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of Sentinel-2 satellite imagery with 13 spectral bands at 10m spatial resolution, processed by THEIA (CNES) with atmospheric correction. Parcel annotations are sourced from the publicly available French Land Parcel Identification System (FLPIS) produced by IGN.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset covers only France and may not generalize to other geographic regions. Temporal sampling is irregular due to cloud filtering and satellite orbit schedules. Approximately 28% of images have at least partial cloud cover. The class nomenclature is limited to 18 crop types; parcels with other crop types are labeled as void. The dataset is highly class-imbalanced.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The 2,433 patches were selected from ~24,000 available patches (10%), favoring patches with rare crop types to reduce class imbalance. The dataset is split into 5 folds for cross-validation, with a 1km buffer between images to avoid cross-fold contamination, and folds are balanced by class distribution (measured by pairwise Kullback-Leibler divergence).
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Atmospheric correction and resampling to 10m/pixel were applied to Sentinel-2 images. Atmospheric bands B01, B09, and B10 were removed, leaving 10 spectral bands. Acquisitions with more than 90% cloud cover were automatically filtered out by the data provider. Patches of 128×128 pixels (1.28×1.28 km) were extracted from 100×100 km Sentinel-2 tiles. A subset of 2,433 patches (10% of all available) was selected, favoring patches with rare crop types to reduce class imbalance.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Remote monitoring of agricultural parcels is necessary for fair allocation of agricultural subsidies (50 and 22 billion euros per year in Europe and the US, respectively) and for ensuring that best crop rotation practices are respected. The dataset enables automated analysis of satellite image time series for applications such as surveying urban development and deforestation.
rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluating panoptic segmentation models on satellite image time series; semantic segmentation of agricultural parcels; crop type mapping; monitoring agricultural land use for subsidy allocation and crop rotation compliance; remote sensing research on temporal dynamics of vegetation.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: The paper does not describe multiple independent annotations per item; annotations come from the FLPIS administrative database, not multiple annotators per item.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotations are derived from the French Land Parcel Identification System (FLPIS) reported by farmers; no annotator demographics are described.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Annotations come from the French LPIS administrative database, not a crowdsourcing or annotation platform.
null_reasons.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Annotations are sourced from the French LPIS administrative database; no machine annotation tools are described for the dataset creation.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains satellite imagery and agricultural parcel annotations; no personal or sensitive information is described.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning, update cadence, or maintenance plan is described in the paper.
null_reasons.inLanguage: The dataset is satellite imagery with numeric pixel values and crop-type labels; it has no natural language content. The 'fr' assignment was based on geographic location (France), not language content of the dataset.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: The zero-padding described is a model training technique applied to batches, not an imputation protocol for the dataset itself. Per Guardrail A, this describes the method, not the dataset.

evidence.name: we present PASTIS, the first open-access SITS dataset with panoptic annotations.
evidence.description: PASTIS is comprised of 2 433 sequences of multi-spectral images of shape 10×128×128. Each sequence contains between 38 and 61 observations taken between September 2018 and November 2019, for a total of over 2 billion pixels.
evidence.url: This dataset, as well as more information about its composition, are publicly available at https://github.com/VSainteuf/pastis-benchmark .

evidence.datePublished: The values reported in this version of the article for the Panoptic Segmentation experiment differ from the version published in the ICCV 2021 proceedings.
evidence.inLanguage: The dataset spans over 4000 km2, with images taken from four different regions of France with diverse climates and crop distributions, covering almost 1% of the French Metropolitan territory.
evidence.citeAs: The values reported in this version of the article for the Panoptic Segmentation experiment differ from the version published in the ICCV 2021 proceedings.
evidence.isLiveDataset: We present PASTIS (Panoptic Agricultural Satellite TIme Series), the first large-scale, publicly available SITS dataset with both semantic and panoptic annotations.
evidence.rai:dataCollection: The PASTIS dataset is composed of 2433 square 128×128 patches with 10 spectral bands and at 10m resolution, obtained from the open-access Sentinel-2 platform. For each patch, we stack all available acquisitions between September 2018 and November 2019, forming our four dimensional multi-spectral SITS.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Each sequence contains between 38 and 61 observations taken between September 2018 and November 2019, for a total of over 2 billion pixels.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionType: The PASTIS dataset is composed of 2433 square 128×128 patches with 10 spectral bands and at 10m resolution, obtained from the open-access Sentinel-2 platform. The publicly available French Land Parcel Identification System (FLPIS) allows us to retrieve the extent and content of all parcels within the tiles, as reported by the farmers.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Each pixel is characterized by 13 spectral bands. We select all bands except the atmospheric bands B01, B09, and B10. The satellite images used in PASTIS were gathered from THEIA: "Value-added data processed by the CNES for the Theia data cluster using Copernicus data."
evidence.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The 10 channels correspond to the non-atmospheric spectral bands of the Sentinel-2 satellite, after atmospheric correction and re-sampling at a spatial resolution of 10 meters per pixel. Each of these tiles is subdivided in square patches of size 1.28×1.28km (128×128 pixels at 10m/pixel), for a total of around 24,000 patches. We then select 2,433 patches (10% of all available patches, see Figure 6b), favoring patches with rare crop types in order to decrease the otherwise extreme class imbalance of the dataset.
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The publicly available French Land Parcel Identification System (FLPIS) allows us to retrieve the extent and content of all parcels within the tiles, as reported by the farmers. Each patch pixel is annotated with a semantic label corresponding to either the parcels' crop type or the background class. The pixels of each unique parcel in the patch receive a corresponding instance label.
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The French Payment Agency estimates the accuracy of the crop annotations via in situ control over 98% and the relative error in terms of surfaces under 0.3%.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: This lack of regularity is due to the automatic filtering of acquisitions with extensive cloud cover by the satellite data provider THEIA. We estimate that close to 28% of images have at least partial cloud cover.
evidence.rai:dataImputationProtocol: we append all-zeroes images at the end of shorter sequences to match the length of the longer sequence in the batch. We retain a padding mask to prevent the spatial and temporal encoding of padded values, and to exclude these padded values from temporal averages.
evidence.rai:dataBiases: As is common in remote sensing applications, the dataset is highly unbalanced, with a ratio of over 50 between the most and least common classes. We then select 2,433 patches (10% of all available patches), favoring patches with rare crop types in order to decrease the otherwise extreme class imbalance of the dataset.
evidence.rai:dataLimitations: The temporal sampling of the sequences in PASTIS is irregular: depending on their location, patches are observed a different number of times and at different intervals. This is a result of both the orbit schedule of Sentinel-2 and the policy of Sentinel data providers not to process tile observations identified as covered by clouds for more than 90% of the tile's surface.
evidence.rai:dataUseCases: We present PASTIS (Panoptic Agricultural Satellite TIme Series), the first large-scale, publicly available SITS dataset with both semantic and panoptic annotations. Crop mapping—the driving application of this paper—relies on exploiting such temporal patterns and entails major financial and environmental stakes.
evidence.rai:dataSocialImpact: remote monitoring of the surface and nature of agricultural parcels is necessary for a fair allocation of agricultural subsidies (50 and 22 billion euros per year in Europe and in the US, respectively) and for ensuring that best crop rotation practices are respected. More generally, the automated analysis of SITS represents a significant interest for a wide range of applications, such as surveying urban development and deforestation.
evidence.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: We then select 2,433 patches (10% of all available patches, see Figure 6b), favoring patches with rare crop types in order to decrease the otherwise extreme class imbalance of the dataset. To allow for cross-validation, the dataset is split into 5 folds, chosen with a 1km buffer between images to avoid cross-fold contamination.
